subject: Can I use RMediation to get confidence interval for indirect effect using DWLS estimator

messages.author: 4d60065baa5c0933
messages.subject: Can I use RMediation to get confidence interval for indirect effect using DWLS estimator
parts:
Hello, 

I'm running multigroup SEM with categorical indicators and DVs in lavaan. Lavaan can not get bootstrap results in such a situation. 
However, the reviewer asks for bootstrap. I was wondering whether I can use the regression coefficients in lavaan output and RMediation package to get the CI for indirect effects and explain the reliability of this result. 

I also define the indirect effects using multiplication of the two coefficients and get the estimates of these defined parameters. which output (lavaan vs. RMediation) would be less biased? 
 Thank you all!

Yikang. Zhang

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Can I use RMediation to get confidence interval for indirect effect using DWLS estimator
parts: I'm running multigroup SEM with categorical indicators and DVs in lavaan. Lavaan can not get bootstrap results in such a situation.

Yes it does.  Do you get an error because some bootstraps fail?  If you have few few observations in certain categories, you can end up estimating different thresholds across bootstrap samples, which means those estimates are not comparable, even though the indirect effect might very well be (we could use a simulation to verify that).
However, the reviewer asks for bootstrap.

Let them know the Monte Carlo CI method has the same advantages as bootstrapping, without being computationally intensive or failing because of sparse categories.  See the ?semTools::monteCarloMed help page for examples and the reference to cite.
I was wondering whether I can use the regression coefficients in lavaan output and RMediation package to get the CI for indirect effects and explain the reliability of this result.

I think so, because that package also implements the Monte Carlo method (as well as the delta method that lavaan implements by default, which assumes asymptotic normality, unlike bootstrapping or the Monte Carlo method).
I also define the indirect effects using multiplication of the two coefficients and get the estimates of these defined parameters. which output (lavaan vs. RMediation) would be less biased?

Depends what you requested.  The default delta-method CIs are mostly likely to be biased, but they won't be in sufficiently large samples.  Monte Carlo CIs only assume the estimated direct-effects themselves have normal sampling distributions, which is met in even modest samples.  Bootstrapping is even less restrictive because it doesn't assume even the direct effects have normal sampling distributions, but in samples small enough for that advantage to become noticeable, bootstrapping also suffers because it is based on a small sample that is less likely to be a good representative of the population than a larger sample.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
